title: Incident Triage Compact Cards with Prioritized Trace Summaries & Runbook Actions
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: During high-severity incidents the on-call workflow requires quickly understanding a service degradation: relevant traces, likely root cause signals, and actionable runbook steps. Current PagerDuty and Slack PD cards are verbose or scatter context across multiple links, increasing mean time to acknowledge/mitigate.

Goal: Ship a compact incident triage card that surfaces a prioritized 1-3 line natural language summary synthesized from span samples, a minimal set of relevant logs/metric links, suggested immediate runbook actions (with single-click Slack buttons), and an encoded context blob (trace ids + short KV) for follow-up. Cards should be compatible with PagerDuty webhooks and Slack incident channels, support both manual and auto-generated postmortem seeds, and respect data access controls for private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: PD webhook payloads include 'triage_card' field with summary, top_trace_id, severity_hint, and suggested_actions
Slack incident messages render compact card with action buttons that trigger documented runbook steps
Clicking an action posts a prefilled incident timeline entry and optionally opens a provisional rollback/mitigation PR template
Card generation completes within 250ms added latency to PD webhook processing under normal load
All sensitive identifiers honor VPC deployment masking rules and KMS-access gating for Private customers
E2E tests verifying trace-to-card mapping and button action flows exist in CI
design_notes: We will compute a lightweight triage summary using an extraction pipeline: sample up to 3 representative spans using weighted-span-selector heuristics, extract error messages and top-3 log lines, then run a constrained summarizer model (on-host small LLM) with deterministic prompt to produce 1-3 sentence summary and 3 ranked suggested actions. Keep payload minimal: use precomputed snippets stored in KV store and include only trace ids + short hash in the PD/Slack payloads. Use adaptive sampling rates to avoid extra load during high-throughput incidents.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'triage-compact-cards' gated by org. 2) Launch to Redwood internal SRE team for 1 week; collect metrics and qualitative feedback. 3) Gradual rollout by org size: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2 weeks. 4) Monitor false-positive action rates and button click-to-resolution conversion, revert if degradation in MTTR observed.
telemetry: Emit events: triage_card.generated, triage_card.rendered, triage_action.clicked (with action_id), triage_card.failure. Capture generation latency distribution, sample trace_ids for downstream debugging (masked in Private), and create Grafana dashboard: triage_card success rate, avg generation latency, actions-per-incident, and time-to-first-click.

2026-03-06: Engineering spike completed. Local summarizer model (quantized 4-bit) fits latency and memory targets. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567

2026-03-10: Integration test added for PD webhook format; observed 180ms median card gen latency in staging. Moving to broader canary next week. Assigned follow-ups for postmortem seed templating and analytics tagging.
